brief.topic: Launch an AI feature as opt-in or on by default?
brief.audience: PMs planning an AI feature launch
constraints: Illustrative numbers labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Opt-in launches only hear from enthusiasts and hide quality problems, so go default-on when wrong answers are cheap, reversible and have a fallback.

hooks.text: Opt-in AI hides its own failures.
Opt-in or on by default? Decide by the cost of being wrong.
hooks.notes: Clear but too long for frame 0.

hooks.text: Your opt-in users aren’t your users.
hooks.notes: Catchy but vague about the decision.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): reframes a launch default PMs rarely question, and the reel ends with a four-part rule.

caption.opening: Opt-in feels like the safe way to launch an AI feature. It’s also the best way to miss its failures.
body: Opt-in users are self-selected enthusiasts. Their feedback flatters you, and the edge cases never show up. (The 4% in the reel is illustrative.)

Go on by default only if:
→ a wrong answer is cheap to spot and undo
→ users can switch back in one click
→ your eval set looks like real traffic
→ unsure answers fall back to the old flow
Miss one? Start opt-in, then deliberately test with users who didn’t choose it.
caption.cta: Share this with your launch team.

claims.text: Opt-in AI launches over-represent enthusiastic users and can hide quality problems; default-on is appropriate when errors are cheap, reversible and have a fallback.
